prompt:
Use case: ui-mockup.
Create a highly polished FOUR-FRAME desktop website interaction storyboard in a 2 by 2 grid, wide landscape board about 1800x1300. This is the NEXT SECTION and its gentle scroll transition for the 8x social minimal website shown in reference image 1. Each panel is a real wide desktop viewport, not mobile, with legible typography and generous whitespace. Reference is design continuity, not an edit target. Match the original serif 8x social logo, warm near-white #F8F8F5, near-black #141414, a tiny amount of vermilion #F44725. Consistent header and margins in ALL panels. Zero additional colours. All panel labels and explanatory captions OUTSIDE the website frames, set elegantly on a very light neutral board background. Board heading 'One page. One clear story.' small but readable, not part of website. Four frames should feel like successive screenshots of the exact same implemented component, not four different designs.
Core next section: heading 'One brief. A whole network.' large but smaller than the hero headline. Single supporting sentence 'We build and manage your creator network, from the first brief to the final post.' Clean 2-column layout underneath: left three generously spaced horizontal accordion rows with hairline dividers, titles 'You set the direction.', 'We find your people.', 'Your network goes live.' Small orange circular dot at the active row; inactive rows have small grey circular dots. Only selected row expands one sentence. Right a single spacious visual area that changes with the selected step. Simple print-like graphic treatment, flat, restrained, no stacked floating UI, no faux app chrome. No background decoration. Same page height for each state. The graphic is explanatory, not a fake functioning product screenshot.
Frame 1 label outside: '01 / SCROLL — The story continues'. Show natural scroll between approved hero and next section: fixed slim header at top, only the bottom portion of the existing static five-person monochrome portrait banner near top of viewport, beneath it generous warm-white breathing space and the next heading 'One brief. A whole network.' with first accordion rows beginning below. It is visibly the same warm-white page, ordinary continuous document scroll. Image does not morph into particles, tilt, or enlarge. No enormous blank space, no colour wipe. The photographic group comes directly from the hero reference.
Frame 2 label outside: '02 / BRIEF — One clear starting point'. Show next section fully visible, hero image naturally above viewport. First accordion active, expanded sentence 'Tell us your goals, audience and brand.' The right visual is one elegant off-white rectangular printed brief sheet with a hairline border and a small orange dot, no shadow. Sheet has the text 'Your brief' and three readable purposeful lines 'Goals', 'Audience', 'Brand', subtle grey rules following each, no fabricated data. Two or three tiny aligned circles along its lower edge suggest a network. Very minimal, beautiful scale.
Frame 3 label outside: '03 / PEOPLE — Select a step'. Identical layout/headings/header/accordion. Now middle row active, expanded sentence 'We source and brief creators who fit your brand.' Right visual replaces brief with three beautifully cropped monochrome portrait circles of people from the existing hero photo, connected by one delicate thin dotted horizontal line with a single orange node. These are small and intentional, not a second giant image collage. Generous white space. A quiet cursor at the second row communicates click, not a big cartoon hand.
Frame 4 label outside: '04 / PUBLISH — The outcome stays clear'. Identical layout. Third row active, expanded sentence 'Creators publish. We manage content and track performance.' Right visual becomes three slim portrait-format outlined post frames, each containing a monochrome creator image from the reference, with a very small bottom black play triangle. No social platform logos, fake metrics, charts, likes or feed chrome. One orange dot on a thin horizontal connecting line below. Editorial and understandable in one glance.
At board bottom only, outside frames, tiny concise design note: 'Natural scroll. Static photography. One active step. 250 ms transitions.' This is a storyboard proposal, not a motion blur illustration. Everything aligns, calm confident grotesk type, minimal interface, strong editorial execution. No gradients, 3D renders, huge coloured sections, glowing networks, decorative slogans, chapter labels in website, scroll instructions in website, clutter, overlap, cinematic wipes, loading effects or colour changes. The primary purpose is showing how a clear simple section can be interactive without feeling like entering a different website.
